title: Service-class Minimum Throughput Orchestrator and Predictive Burst Shedder
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation:
We need predictable minimum throughput for differentiated service classes (e.g. Gold/Silver/Bronze) on Dedicated fleets while preserving overall fleet efficiency. Short bursts from low-priority tenants can cause headroom exhaustion and SLA regressions for higher classes. This PR introduces a service-class minimum-throughput orchestrator that enforces soft guarantees and a predictive burst shedder that proactively attenuates low-priority bursts when forecasted headroom is insufficient.

What this PR does (overview):
- Introduces ServiceClassMinThroughput controller that computes per-service-class soft throughput floors based on reservation commitments and recent utilization curves. Floors are enforced by a light-weight admission filter in the fleet gateway.
- Adds a PredictiveBurstShedder: a fast, locality-aware component that samples short-term utilization forecasts (p95 headroom over next 30s) and issues transient shed signals targeted at low-priority burst tokens. This avoids global pool preemption and keeps Gold-class latency stable.
- Telemetry: exposes new metrics (redwood.service_class.min_throughput, redwood.service_class.predicted_headroom_pct, redwood.burst_shed.actions_total, redwood.burst_shed.shed_latency_ms) and labels for service_class and pool_id.
- Config & rollout: new config schema (fleet.capacity.service_classes[]) with min_throughput_pct and prediction_window_sec. Default preserves existing behavior (min_throughput_pct=0).
- Tests & perf: unit tests for controller math and admission filter; end-to-end sim harness with synthetic workloads (80/15/5 Gold/Silver/Bronze) demonstrating stable 99th-latency for Gold under bursty patterns. Included load-test artifacts and dashboards.

Detailed changes (single-line summaries):
- controller/service_class_min_throughput.go: core algorithm + smoothing, commitment projection, hysteresis
- gateway/admission_filter.go: integrates per-request service_class lookup and enforcement path
- shedder/predictive_shedder.go: forecasting + shed decision + targeted token invalidation API
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go: metric definitions and labels
- config/fleet_schema_v2.yaml: schema additions and examples
- e2e/sim/throughput_guarantee_test.go: harness and scenarios
- docs/ops/service_classes.md: operator-facing rollout and tuning guide

Why this is different from existing autoscale work:
Existing hedging/autoscale PRs focus on headroom allocation and warm-pool sizing at the cluster level. This change is orthogonal: it enforces per-service-class minimums and intentionally sheds only bursts that are low-priority and forecasted to cause SLA slippage. The emphasis is protection of latency SLOs for premium tenants while still allowing opportunistic utilization elsewhere.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag default-off with config schema available.
2) Canary on small subset of Dedicated fleets (Gold-enabled only) and monitor new metrics (predicted_headroom_pct and shed_actions_total).
3) Gradual enable by increasing min_throughput_pct for Gold; keep Silver/Bronze at 0 to observe impact.
4) After 2 weeks of stability, flip default to on for all Dedicated fleets with conservative thresholds.

Notes for reviewers:
- The admission filter path is intentionally minimal to keep added median latency < 20us; see microbenchmarks in controller/benchmarks.md.
- Prediction model is simple EWMA + short linear extrapolation to keep false positives low; can be replaced later with more advanced predictors.
- We decided against hard preemption of long-lived requests; the shedder only invalidates ephemeral burst tokens and signals the gateway to return 429-like hints for best-effort clients.

Sofia Alvarez (2026-02-12): Please add more unit coverage around the hysteresis boundary to avoid flip-flopping under oscillatory load.
Maya Chen (2026-02-12): Added tests and increased smoothing alpha; see commit d19e7aa and e9a3d55.
